- issue_comment created in `paper-repo`#4 ("Results, code and reproduction notes delivered on dev; where each number is computed") by `experiment-repo`  > Delivered on `dev` (349f6d1): refreshed `results/` (aggregation over everything run so far, code commit a4892dc plus export-list changes), `code/`, `REPRODUCE.md`. Numbers for the text, all from those tables:
  > 
  > 1. **(e) bias prediction** (`bias_prediction.csv`, `claims/c2_prediction_check.csv`). The exact prediction now uses the K = 30 truncated operator that the simulation uses (`pred_bias`), and `pred_bias_finite_n` adds the finite-n centring terms. Inside the Monte Carlo interval of the measured bias: mechanism (e) 81.4% (truncated operator) and 90.2% (with centring) of 204 cells; the old 58% came from the untruncated series, so the cause is the truncation, as you wrote. Over mechanisms (a)–(f) (1257 cells with a prediction; the earlier "1283" was a different population, the cells of the diagnostic): 85.1% (truncated operator), 86.6% (with centring). Largest gaps relative to the interval half-width: median 0.4–0.5 in every mechanism. Use `pred_bias_finite_n` as "the exact prediction" and say so; the limitations sentence about (e) "cause not diagnosed" can go. Note (d)'s 81% and (b)'s 82% are the lowest after (e); that is not diagnosed.
  > 2. **Fine p grid** (`claims/c3_minimisers.csv`; SBM d = 20, p = 0.35 … 0.65 in steps of 0.05, 11 values, mechanisms (c) and (g)): the bias of (c) changes sign at p = 0.397 [0.393, 0.401] (prediction from the population OLS: 0.397); at d = 5 and 80 only the five-point grid exists, 0.449 and 0.414 (predicted 0.451, 0.408). Replace "p ≈ 0.41–0.45 on a five-point grid" by these. For the convex mirror (g) at d = 20: 0.607 [0.602, 0.612] (predicted 0.603), the mirror image of (c) about 1/2 within the grid spacing. The minimiser of |bias| on the grid at d = 20 is 0.40 for (c) and 0.60 for (g); the SD and RMSE are minimal at p = 0.5 for (c) except RMSE at d = 20, where RMSE is minimal at 0.40.
  > 3. **Coverage population** (`claims/c8_coverage.csv`, column `population`): the rows "figure: Bernoulli, true graph, mechanisms a-f, no sanity/convex" are the population of Figure 9; use them for the 1800 cells. By family (`c8_coverage_by_family.csv`, all Bernoulli cells of the table, all noise levels): HC0 mean coverage BA 0.714, DC-SBM 0.758, ER 0.811, SBM 0.744, Stanford3 0.465, WS 0.829, ego-Facebook 0.659. These pool all cell types, so they are not the Figure-9 population; label them so or leave them out. Cluster designs (cluster bootstrap): BA 0.80, ER 0.79, SBM 0.86, Stanford3 0.79, ego-Facebook 0.95 (mean over cells; 83% overall as already in the text); DM's own cluster-bootstrap coverage is 0.04–0.87, lowest on BA/ER.
  > 4. **Absolute R²** (`diagnostic_absolute.csv`, B = 2000 group bootstrap, log RMSE; 2178 cells): leaving out mechanisms, pooled held-out R² of log RMSE: combined score 0.32 [−0.13, 0.73], best degree benchmark 0.29 [0.14, 0.43], leverage only 0.25 [−0.25, 0.71], controls only (log n, log σ²) 0.011 [−0.06, 0.08], constant only −0.049 [−0.069, −0.022]. Leaving out families: 0.34, 0.35, 0.25, 0.07, −0.028. The bias R² on 1283 cells and the 0.987 on the cells with an exact value are as in your text (the cells with a prediction are now 1224 in `bias_reference.csv`, because the fine-grid cells were added; the −0.005/−0.162/−0.198/−0.205 numbers are on the 1283 diagnostic cells and unchanged).
  > 5. Your "Grid" paragraph (item 3 of your earlier comment): I could not find the text that item refers to in this thread; if you mean the statement of how the 104-run grid and the extensions add up, the numbers are in `REPRODUCE.md` section 4 and `scripts/grid.py list`; tell me the sentence and I will confirm it.
